description: EU-wide core funding programmes for AI and digitalisation projects, applicable to organisations in EU member states and associated countries

programmes.summary_en: The EU's flagship R&D and innovation programme supporting companies, universities and research organisations. Covers AI, data, digitalisation, deep-tech, and sustainability projects across multiple thematic clusters.
programmes.funding_rate_en: Up to 70-100% (depending on call, action type, and participant role)
programmes.max_amount_en: Typically from €500k up to €10m+ per project (varies by call)
programmes.notes_en: 2026–27 work programme adopted in December 2025 (€14bn overall); first calls open since 16 Dec 2025 via the Funding & Tenders Portal.

programmes.summary_en: Supports deployment and uptake of digital technologies including AI, advanced digital skills, high-performance computing, cybersecurity, and data spaces across the EU.
programmes.max_amount_en: Typically up to several million euros per project
programmes.notes_en: Focus on deployment rather than research. 2026 calls (Advanced Digital Skills, Best Use of Technologies, GenAI/AI Continent) open since April 2026.

programmes.summary_en: Part of the European Innovation Council, providing equity and grants for high-risk, high-impact innovation projects. Particularly suited for AI-driven business models and deep-tech scale-ups.
programmes.funding_rate_en: Up to €2.5m grant component + equity investment up to ~€15m
programmes.notes_en: Highly competitive. 2026: six full-proposal cut-offs (7 Jan, 4 Mar, 6 May, 8 Jul, 2 Sep, 4 Nov 2026); short proposal (Step 1) can be submitted anytime. Grant up to €2.5m as lump sum.

programmes.summary_en: Supports early-stage development of breakthrough technologies through collaborative research. Ideal for ambitious AI research with transformative potential.
programmes.notes_en: Focus on visionary research. Consortium required for Open calls; single applicants possible for Challenges. 2026: Open deadline was 12 May 2026 (closed); Challenges close 28 Oct 2026 — incl. 'DeepRAP' trustworthy cognitive AI challenge (up to €4m per project).

programmes.summary_en: The European Social Fund Plus supports training, upskilling, and reskilling in digital and AI-related competencies across EU member states.
programmes.max_amount_en: Typically up to several hundred thousand euros per project
programmes.notes_en: Implemented through national/regional programmes. Contact national ESF managing authority for specific calls.

programmes.summary_en: European Investment Bank instruments providing loans, guarantees, and equity for innovative companies, including AI and digital technology ventures.
programmes.notes_en: Legacy initiative of the Horizon 2020 period (2014–2020) — new financing runs via InvestEU and current EIB Group instruments; check the InvestEU portal for available products. Access typically through local financial intermediaries.

programmes.summary_en: Joint programme supporting international collaborative R&D projects led by innovative SMEs. Covers all technology areas including AI and digitalisation.
programmes.funding_rate_en: Up to 50-70% (varies by national funding body)
programmes.notes_en: Requires partners from at least 2 Eurostars countries; SME must lead the consortium. Call 11: submissions 9 Jul–10 Sep 2026 (14:00 CET) via myeurekaproject.org; funding via national bodies.

programmes.summary_en: Supports cross-border, transnational and interregional cooperation projects, including digital transformation and smart specialisation initiatives.
programmes.funding_rate_en: Up to 70-85% (depending on programme and region)
programmes.notes_en: Multiple programmes covering different geographic areas. Partners from multiple regions/countries required.
